描述_EN: fire-gilding is now banned in most countries because the mercury vapour is not only toxic to the person undertaking the gilding, it also escapes into the atmosphere. a small amount of gold was left adhering to the base metal and the method was particularly suited to the application of very thin layers. it has 'gold splash' decoration. censers were part of sets of altar vessels in use in chinese temples. the process could be repeated many times to build up layers of gold. this bronze censer has a rectangular body meant to be formed of four peaches, their stems forming its handles. this involves applying gold in the form of a gold/mercury amalgam and then heating the vessel to drive off the mercury. this would have been achieved by fire-gilding.
描述_ZN: 火镀金现在在大多数国家都被禁止了，因为汞蒸汽不仅对从事镀金的人有毒，它还会逃逸到大气中。 少量的金子被留在基底金属上，这种方法特别适合于应用非常薄的层。 它有 "溅金 "装饰。 香炉是中国寺庙中使用的成套祭器的一部分。 这个过程可以重复多次，以建立黄金的层次。 这个青铜香炉有一个长方形的身体，是由四个桃子组成的，它们的茎形成了它的手柄。 这涉及到以金/汞汞合金的形式涂抹黄金，然后加热容器以驱除汞。 这应该是通过火镀金实现的。
